reason: The current goal is to make supporting material, so I’ll start with the copied collagen instructions and protein machinery.
expectation: I expect the machinery to use the instructions toward making collagen, though amino acids may be needed next.

alternatives.reason: Surface renewal also seems relevant to repair, but supporting material is the stated goal.

effect: The copied instructions direct the repair cells’ protein builders toward making collagen, so amino acids seem like the next useful input.
reaction: The link back to the muscle cells’ similar machinery is interesting.
reason: Amino acids are the building blocks needed to make the supporting protein.
expectation: I expect the directed builders to use the amino acids to make collagen or a precursor that needs further processing.

alternatives.reason: Surface renewal also matters for repair, but I want to finish making the supporting material first.

effect: The amino acids became collagen chains; the chains appear to need processing before they can support the damaged site.
reaction: It is useful to see how instructions, materials and energy each contribute.
reason: Processing and export seem like the next step toward usable supporting material.
expectation: I expect the collagen chains to be processed and exported, though they may still need to be assembled into fibers.

alternatives.reason: Surface renewal is relevant, but I want to continue making the supporting material first.

effect: The collagen material has been processed and exported, so it seems ready to be assembled into supporting fibers.
reaction: The distinction between making a protein and delivering it is useful.
reason: Fiber-forming helpers seem suited to turning the exported precursors into supporting material.
expectation: I expect the precursors to form collagen fibers that can help support the damaged site.

alternatives.reason: Surface renewal also matters, but I want to finish the supporting material first.

effect: The exported material has formed collagen fibers outside the cells, ready to support the damaged site.
reaction: It is interesting that the cells' work creates structure beyond their own boundaries.
reason: Adding the new fibers to the body should advance the current goal of supporting the damaged site.
expectation: I expect the fibers to help rebuild support at the scrape, though the surface may still need renewal.

alternatives.reason: Surface renewal also seems relevant, but I want to use the supporting fibers first.

effect: The new fibers have been laid down at the damaged site, completing the supporting-material goal; surface coverage is next.
reaction: The distinction between a temporary seal and rebuilt tissue is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it directly addresses surface renewal.
expectation: I expect the signals to prompt resident surface cells to renew coverage, perhaps with another step needed to close the scrape.

effect: The signals prompted existing surface cells to move and multiply, making them ready to cover the repair.
reaction: It is useful to distinguish a renewal signal from the cells and materials that do the rebuilding.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should put the spreading cells over the damaged area.
expectation: I expect the cells to restore surface coverage over the scrape, though the tissue may still need time to reorganize.

effect: Surface coverage has been restored, though deeper rebuilding continues; the next goal is to lift and hold the glass.
reaction: The possibility of a scar makes the repair feel less like an instant reset.
reason: This is the only offered combination and directly addresses the new goal.
expectation: I expect the body to lift and hold the glass, drawing on the muscle, control and supply systems built earlier.

effect: The body can lift and hold the glass while its muscles, nerves, circulation and repaired skin continue working; the chapter is complete.
reaction: The return to holding the glass ties the earlier systems together in a satisfying way.

mostWorthwhile.text: Lifting and holding the glass made the relationships between cellular energy use, muscle tension, control and blood supply concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence of processing and assembling collagen felt somewhat repetitive, even though it showed distinct stages.

surprise.text: I was struck that cells make supporting fibers outside their own boundaries, and that restored surface coverage can coexist with deeper repair and scarring.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the offered combinations had clear connections to the repair goals, although the menu guided compatibility.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it explored a different body process. The final glass action brought the systems together, though the guided sequence sometimes felt predictable.
